query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: crew_friendliness_warmth
per_column.rationale: The warmth/friendliness of cabin crew is a genuine sub-aspect OF an airline's service offering, which is itself a pillar of competitive advantage. It is an attribute of the concept, not an external driver of it.

per_column.name: crew_attentiveness_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Attentiveness/responsiveness of crew is a distinct in-flight service dimension and thus a constitutive aspect of competitive advantage. It overlaps somewhat with crew_friendliness (both are 'cabin crew service'), but captures a different behavioural axis (helpfulness/speed vs. warmth).

per_column.name: seat_comfort_legroom
per_column.rationale: Seat comfort and legroom is a hard-product/cabin dimension along which airlines compete, i.e. an aspect OF the competitive advantage, not a predictor of it.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Catering quality is a recognised service/product dimension that partly constitutes an airline's advantage; it is a part-of aspect of the concept.

per_column.name: ground_staff_service
per_column.rationale: Ground service (check-in, gate, handling) is a distinct service touchpoint and a legitimate constitutive facet of the overall competitive advantage, non-overlapping with in-flight crew touchpoints.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are genuine part-of aspects of an airline's competitive advantage (service warmth, service responsiveness, seat/hardware comfort, catering, ground service) rather than external predictors, causes, or restatements, so the part-of/meronymy claim is satisfied. Mutual exclusivity is high but not perfect: the two crew columns (friendliness vs. attentiveness) both live under the 'cabin crew service' aspect and can co-vary, and crew vs. ground staff both fall under the broader 'service' banner, creating mild redundancy risk. Exhaustiveness is only moderate: the set carves the 'service + comfort + food' portion of competitive advantage well, but omits several major constitutive facets of airline competitive advantage such as price/value-for-money, inflight entertainment, on-time performance/reliability, network/route connectivity, baggage handling, and boarding/check-in efficiency. Because it covers roughly half of the concept's constitutive dimensions, exhaustiveness is scored around 0.55.
